description: Deliver WO-B3 as an end-to-end provider discovery CLI slice: make `you providers list` available through the canonical injected process and report deterministic provider identity, availability/prerequisites, models, effort settings, modalities, tools, and named known limits in aligned human, JSON, help, and reference surfaces without live provider calls or a second catalog.

context.customerAsk: Make `you providers list` available from the canonical root.BuildProcess and Process.Execute path and enumerate every first-party provider's canonical identity, availability/prerequisites, models, effort settings, input/output modalities, tools, and known limits. Ensure operators can discover before execution that gpt-5.6 lacks video/audio understanding, image generation accepts at most five referenced image paths, and ANTIGRAVITY/AGY accepts video/audio file paths with its supported models/efforts and documented --add-dir/timeout constraints. Keep human, JSON, help, and reference behavior aligned and prove the command without live provider calls.
context.problem: The installed CLI rejects `you providers list` even though the Providers root, catalog contracts, model-provider manifests, and Providers-owned list/show adapters already exist. The incomplete public path and incomplete capability metadata force operators to discover modality mismatches and hard provider limits through failed or misleading production runs.
context.solution: Extend the existing authored model-provider catalog with validated provider/model discovery facts, project them through the Providers root, render deterministic equivalent human and JSON output through the Providers CLI transport, register that transport in the canonical CLI manifest and pkg/wire process graph, align help/reference guidance, and add focused plus root.BuildProcess/Process.Execute regression evidence. Do not add another registry, injector, runtime path, local-model harness, storage engine, or media transform.

acceptanceCriteria: `you providers list` succeeds through the production root.BuildProcess and Process.Execute path and enumerates every first-party provider exactly once without constructing a second service graph or making a live provider call.

Each provider entry reports canonical identity, availability/readiness and sanitized prerequisites, supported models, allowed effort settings, input/output modalities, tools, and named known limits in deterministic order.

The inventory makes these facts directly discoverable before execution: gpt-5.6 has no video or audio understanding; image generation accepts at most five referenced image paths; and ANTIGRAVITY/AGY accepts video and audio file paths with its supported models/efforts plus documented --add-dir and timeout constraints.
Human output and --json output represent the same canonical facts; command help and `you docs providers` explain the fields and usage without contradicting the catalog.

Unknown command/argument, catalog validation, mapping, unavailable-prerequisite, and output-write failures retain established CLI behavior, keep data on the correct output channel, and emit safe structured diagnostics without sensitive values.

Typecheck, focused tests, required generation checks, and required CI pass with no NEW lint violations relative to current main, and the gates green on main (backend-size, pkg-maint, pkg-file-count, pkg-structure, vet) stay green.

The implementation/review loop continues until required CI is terminal and passing, all blocking PR conversation feedback is explicitly addressed, merge conflicts and shared/generated-file churn are reconciled, and the PR is actually merged.

userStories.title: Publish canonical provider capability facts
userStories.description: As an operator selecting a provider and model, I want the Providers catalog to return complete execution-planning facts so that all discovery surfaces use one trustworthy authority.
acceptanceCriteria: Listing the canonical catalog returns every first-party provider exactly once with canonical identity, support/implementation availability, readiness prerequisites, supported models, effort settings, input modalities, output modalities, tools, and named known limits.

The Codex/gpt-5.6 data explicitly represents text/image support as applicable and the absence of video and audio understanding; its image-generation limit states that at most five referenced image paths are accepted.

The ANTIGRAVITY entry identifies AGY and advertises its supported AGY model names and effort values, video/audio file-path input, required AGY executable/auth/workspace prerequisites, workspace extension through --add-dir, and the documented print-timeout behavior/limit.
Claude and every other first-party entry expose the same field shape with truthful empty or explicit unsupported values rather than omitted ambiguity.

Catalog decoding rejects invalid identities, duplicate provider/model facts, unknown modality/direction or effort values, malformed/non-positive numeric limits, and incomplete named-limit records with actionable errors.
Returned catalog values are detached from the embedded source and have deterministic provider, model, modality, effort, tool, prerequisite, and limit ordering.

Authored model-provider manifests remain the authority; generated catalog/schema/type artifacts are regenerated from them only where the accepted public catalog contract changes, and generated files are not hand-edited.
Focused authored-catalog, schema/contract, projection, clone-safety, ordering, and invalid-manifest tests pass.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Implemented authored model-provider capability facts and generated schema/catalog/package artifacts for Codex, Claude, and Antigravity; projected deterministic, clone-safe Providers descriptors with sanitized prerequisites, models, efforts, modalities, tools, and known limits. Focused catalog/projection/provider tests, provider-catalog and package generation checks, API validation, affected Go packages, and UI typecheck pass. The repository-wide make test target still reports the unrelated existing TestMockWorkersSchema_StaleStagingDetectedByContractCheck failure for stale packages/api artifacts.

userStories.title: Render stable provider discovery output
userStories.description: As an operator, I want `providers list` output to be complete, readable, and scriptable so that I can compare providers or automate preflight checks without invoking one.
acceptanceCriteria: The Providers-owned CLI list operation renders each provider and its models, effort settings, directional modalities, tools, prerequisites, and named limits in a stable, documented human-readable layout with no dependence on input map or slice order.
--json emits a stable structured envelope containing the same canonical facts as human output, preserves typed values such as numeric maxima, and writes no human table text to stdout.
Both formats visibly encode unsupported/empty capabilities so gpt-5.6's lack of video/audio understanding cannot be mistaken for unknown metadata.
Both formats make the five-referenced-image-path limit and ANTIGRAVITY/AGY video/audio file-path, model/effort, --add-dir, and timeout facts discoverable by stable names and descriptions.

List rendering uses only the injected Providers service operation, performs no environment discovery or provider execution, and emits safe request/success/failure verbose diagnostics to stderr while keeping stdout machine-safe.
Context cancellation, Providers service failures, and output-write failures return errors without fabricated success diagnostics or leaking sensitive provider/process details.
Focused mapping, human/JSON parity, deterministic-ordering, empty/unsupported, cancellation, service-failure, and writer-failure tests pass.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Expose and verify the canonical public command
userStories.description: As a CLI user, I want `you providers list` to be discoverable and executable from the installed command tree so that provider preflight information is available in the same way as other public CLI operations.
acceptanceCriteria: `you providers list` is present in root and family help, accepts the established global --json and --verbose conventions, rejects unsupported arguments with the standard usage failure, and invokes the Providers-owned CLI adapter.

The thin command entrypoint receives the already-constructed Providers service from the canonical pkg/wire application graph; pkg/initializer only activates injected roles, and command execution performs no child injection, service lookup, provider process call, network call, or runtime-session construction.

`you docs providers` explains how to read models, effort settings, directional modalities, tools, availability/prerequisites, and known limits, and includes the gpt-5.6, five-image-path, and ANTIGRAVITY/AGY operational facts without becoming a second capability authority.

A functional regression constructs the application with root.BuildProcess, runs Process.Execute with `providers list` and `providers list --json`, and proves successful output includes all required facts and deterministic provider ordering without live provider calls.
The same regression proves an unsupported providers subcommand/argument returns established CLI usage behavior and does not emit a successful or partial capability inventory.

CLI manifest/help generated artifacts are updated through the repository generator when their authored command contract changes; unrelated OpenAPI or generated interface artifacts remain unchanged unless an accepted public API contract truly changes.
The independently runnable end-to-end verification command passes: `go test ./tests/functional/providers/discovery/... -run '^TestProvidersListThroughRootBuildProcess$' -count=1`.
Focused root-command, help/manifest, reference smoke, and functional CLI tests pass.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
